like an Excel cell formula, advanced DAX feels random.

visual fields, relationships and DAX filters. Scalar: A single value returned by a measure for the current evaluation.

Row context and filter context sound similar but behave differently. Confusing them causes calculated columns, iterators and measures to
Recognize row context in calculated columns/iterators; recognize filter context in measures/report cells; know that row context does not

5. New words before we use them
Row context: The current row being evaluated, common in calculated columns and iterators. Calculated column: A model column computed row by row and
stored in the model. Measure: A calculation evaluated at query/report time under filter context.

measures see. They can interact, but they are not interchangeable.

In FactSales, calculated column LineAmount = FactSales[Quantity] * FactSales[UnitPrice] uses the current FactSales row.
Measure [Sales] = SUM(FactSales[LineAmount]) does not use one current row; it aggregates rows allowed by filter context.
If you write a calculated column that references a naked aggregate expression, do not assume the current row becomes a filter automatically.
Compare a matrix measure to a calculated column value and state when each is evaluated.
Use measures for interactive aggregations and calculated columns only when a stored row-level attribute is justified.

together. Prefer measures for reusable interactive business metrics; justify stored calculated columns by modeling need.

CALCULATE: Evaluates an expression in a modified filter context. Filter modifier: A DAX function/argument used to remove, keep or alter filter/relationship
behavior. KEEPFILTERS: Changes filter application so new filters intersect with existing filters instead of replacing the same-column filter.

SUM cannot evaluate an expression such as Quantity * UnitPrice row by row unless that value already exists as a column. Iterators solve
this by visiting rows of a table expression.
Use SUMX/AVERAGEX conceptually; state iterator table/grain; distinguish iterator row context from final aggregation; avoid iterating

5. New words before we use them
Iterator: A function ending commonly in X that evaluates an expression for rows of a table, then aggregates results. Table expression: An expression
returning a table of rows for the iterator to visit. SUMX: Iterator that evaluates an expression per row and sums the resulting values.
Iterator measure + row-grain statement + manual check + explain-back. VIDEO: intentionally book-led for this lesson

Assembly line: an iterator takes a table, visits one row at a time, evaluates an expression at that row, then aggregates the produced values. If the
input row grain is wrong, SUMX faithfully totals the wrong thing.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
The iterator table is FactSales; current row is one sales line.
For each allowed fact row, calculate Quantity * UnitPrice; SUMX then adds the row results.
Filter context from Category/Region still determines which FactSales rows enter the iterator.
Validate one small filtered selection by manually summing 3-5 visible rows.

Context transition explains several DAX results that otherwise seem magical. It occurs when CALCULATE converts row context into filter

DAX7 - Period comparison and rolling metrics
YoY, MoM and rolling metrics can mislead when the comparison period is incomplete, denominator is blank/zero, or the rolling window
Build comparison measures in layers: base -> prior period -> absolute difference -> percentage change; then build rolling-window measures
with explicit window definition and completeness rules.

Period-over-period: Comparing a metric with another defined period such as prior month/year. Rolling window: A moving set of recent periods used to
calculate a metric. Comparable period: A prior/current period valid for comparison under the business rule.

without losing orientation. Tooltip, drillthrough and bookmark state are UX contracts, not decoration.

A report interaction map where each feature has one clear purpose and users can always understand how to return/reset.
Interaction choice follows the user's next question rather than feature novelty. Professional upgrade: Treat interaction state as report logic. Changes to
slicers/visuals can invalidate saved bookmark expectations, so interaction QA belongs in release testing.

unintended slicer/filter state. | 4. Cross-highlighting every visual even when it confuses the story.

elements receive keyboard focus. Non-color cue: Text, icon, shape, pattern or position that communicates meaning in addition to color.

C2_04 Module Test - Protected Review RC4
Open only after a saved genuine attempt. Diagnose the weak competency, close this review, then perform a
changed retry.
DAX1
A measure is evaluated inside the active filter context supplied by visual coordinates, slicers, page/report filters, relationships
and DAX filters. Different cells ask different filtered questions.
DAX2
Row context identifies the current row for row-by-row expressions; filter context is the set of allowed values/tables for
measure evaluation. Iterators create row context; measures primarily respond to filter context.
DAX3
CALCULATE evaluates an expression after changing filter context. Describe starting filters, each added/replaced/removed
filter, then the re-evaluated expression.
DAX4
Use an iterator when the expression must be evaluated per row before aggregation, such as Quantity * UnitPrice. Validate
the iterator input table/grain first or it will multiply an already duplicated grain.
DAX5
Context transition converts current-row values into filters when CALCULATE is invoked; measure references can invoke
CALCULATE behavior implicitly. Trace which row columns become filters.
DAX6
Use a trustworthy Date table with unique continuous dates, correct active relationship/role and a base measure that already
reconciles. Then shift the date context and re-evaluate.
DAX7
Define the window anchor, included dates, complete/partial-period policy and comparison period. Boundary months can
contain unequal days/data completeness and silently distort a percentage.
DAX8
Variables label intermediate results and let you temporarily RETURN each piece while debugging. A variable stores the result
from the context where it is defined; later code does not re-evaluate it like a live cell reference.
DAX9
Define eligible population, numerator, denominator, exception/blank-zero treatment and expected total behavior. Then
reconcile numerator/denominator independently.
DAX10
Freeze a failing cell/context; test base measures; expose variables/intermediate tables; compare row/subtotal/grand total and
slicer states; identify the first divergence before rewriting the final formula.
DAX11
A decision-first page establishes one message and evidence hierarchy: headline, trend, drivers, exceptions,
recommendation. Remove visuals that do not change a decision or explain a material exception.
DAX12
Test starting context, navigation trigger, target context/filter state, back/reset route and repeated use. Essential conclusions
must not live only in hover tooltips.
DAX13
Use sufficient contrast, visible labels/text, meaningful alt text, logical keyboard/tab order, non-color encodings and accessible
navigation. Verify critical information remains available without hover.

2. Expected reasoning path
Start by separating facts: Subscription is one subscription, Billing is one subscription-month invoice, MonthlyTargets is one
Plan-Month, and ActiveSnapshot is one Plan-SnapshotDate. Measures must name the fact/grain they summarize.
A naive SUM of ActiveAccounts over the snapshot fact returns 900 across all nine rows. The latest overall snapshot is 309 on
2026-06-28. The correct measure therefore needs a latest-date/semi-additive contract, not just SUM.
The three monthly target totals rise from 186,000 to 201,000. “Current target,” “period target,” and “cumulative target” are
different measures; totals must follow the chosen definition instead of whatever the matrix grand total happens to do.
Billing has exactly three rows for each subscription, and April billed amount happens to equal the all-subscription MRR
control. That coincidence does not make Subscription MRR and Billing Amount the same measure across all periods.
Dynamic RLS user multi.cs@example.com has two mapping rows (East and South). The intended security result is the union
of allowed regions. Test single-region users, the multi-region user, and an unmapped identity before release.

2. Expected reasoning path
Ticket measures must distinguish CreatedDate from ClosedDate. Two resolved tickets close in July even though the target
period stops in June, so a created-period and closed-period chart can legitimately disagree.
The average ResolutionHours is 34.5 for resolved tickets; it also happens to be 34.5 across all 120 rows in this synthetic
fixture. That equality is a trap: prove the Status filter in the DAX/context rather than treating a matching number as validation.
BacklogSnapshot is one Team-SnapshotDate. Summing all four monthly snapshots produces 1,086, but the latest total is
263. A current-backlog KPI must select the intended latest snapshot in context.
Target is one Team-Month. Compare period resolved counts to targets through Team/Date dimensions; never multiply the
target by ticket count.
ops.manager@example.com maps to T01 and T03. RLS should expose the union (34 tickets / 22 resolved in this fixture),
while still denying other teams.

• Uses a grand-total special case instead of a measure that behaves consistently under filters.
• RLS multi-team user shows only one mapping or all teams.
• Accessibility/interaction/lifecycle tests are absent.
